title: WANDERING YEARS UNDER A FAITHFUL GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They left the Desert of Sinai and camped at Kibroth Hattaavah. They left Kibroth Hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth. They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah. They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez. They left Rimmon Perez and camped at Libnah. They left Libnah and camped at Rissah. They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah. They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher. - Num 33:16-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After Sinai, the names come thick and fast — Kibroth Hattaavah, Hazeroth, Rithmah, and on and on. These represent the long years of wilderness wandering, the decades Israel spent moving from camp to camp because the previous generation had refused to trust God and enter the land. In one sense, these were wasted years, the consequence of unbelief. And yet God did not abandon His people even during them.

Some of these places carry painful memories. Kibroth Hattaavah means "graves of craving" — the place where Israel's greedy complaining led to judgment. Hazeroth was where Miriam and Aaron opposed Moses. These were not glorious chapters. But even through Israel's failures and God's discipline, He kept leading, kept providing, kept walking with them stage by stage.

This speaks tenderly to us. Perhaps you look back on seasons that feel like wilderness years — times of wandering, of consequences for poor choices, of slow and painful lessons. Even those years were not beyond God's presence. He does not walk away when we wander. He disciplines those He loves (Heb 12:6), and He remains faithful even when we are faithless (2 Tim 2:13).

The wilderness was not the end of Israel's story, and your wilderness seasons are not the end of yours. God was patiently, faithfully bringing His people toward the land the whole time. In Christ, no season is finally wasted; He can redeem even our wandering years and weave them into His good purpose.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you have "wilderness years" you struggle to make peace with?
2. How does it comfort you that God kept leading Israel even through their wandering?
3. How might God be redeeming your hardest seasons for good?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Patient Lord, thank You that You never abandon me, even in my wandering years. Redeem the wilderness seasons of my life, and lead me faithfully toward the good future You have prepared in Christ. Amen.
